reviews.title: NGUYỄN QUỲNH ANH · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em đã viết đúng đề, đủ 182 từ và đổi cách diễn đạt đề trong mở bài. Cách chia đoạn theo Argentina/Australia rồi Thailand có thể dùng được. Tuy nhiên, Overview nói Australia giảm lại ghi nhầm thành Argentina, còn số cuối của Argentina phải là 466,089, không phải 466,098. Em cũng cần viết rõ nước gắn với 235,088 xe, nêu việc Thailand giảm sau đỉnh năm 2006 và soát lại chủ ngữ, động từ, giới từ trong đoạn cuối. Cô yêu cầu em sửa các điểm này rồi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em dành Detail 1 cho Argentina và Australia, Detail 2 cho Thailand; cách chia theo đối tượng này được chấp nhận. Detail 1 đã cho thấy hai chiều biến động trái ngược qua ba mốc, còn Detail 2 có đủ ba số của Thailand. Em cần gọi tên Argentina ngay ở số đầu, làm rõ Thailand tăng đến 2006 rồi giảm đến 2009 và thêm so sánh trực tiếp tại mốc 2006 để người đọc thấy Argentina đã vượt Australia.

reviews.originalEssay:
The table illustrates how many cars were produced in three countries consist of Argentina, Australia and Thailand over a period of 6 years, commencing from 2003.

Overall, there was a general increase in the amount of cars in Argentina and Thailand also went up; however, not rose continuously, while an opposite trend was observed in the case of Argentina's cars production. Also a note is that cars made in Thailand consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.

To elaborate, in 2003, 235,088 cars were made, with a continuous gradual upward trend to 352,759 cars in 2006 and 466,098 cars in 2009. Starting at 452,163 cars in 2003, the number of cars manufactured in Australia decreased considerably to 341,268 in 2006, followed by a final drop to 245,624 three years later.

Regarding categories with remaining nation, the figures for car productions in Thailand has a remarkable upturn from 735,852 cars in 2003 from 999,963 in 2009. Meanwhile, in the middle of a 6-year period, in 2006, Thailand's cars had the dramatic growth to 1,162,356 cars, remarking the highest point of the table.

This was followed by a decline to 999,963 in 2009, but Thailand still made more than twice as many cars as Argentina that year.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line charts compare the numbers of male and female prisoners in a European country over a century period, commencing from 1911.

Overall, the male prison population was mostly much higher than that of females throughout the years. While the number of male prisoners generally increased, particularly after 1971, the female figures significantly went down during the first half of the studied period and slightly went up towards the end.

Regarding men, there were around 18,000 male prisoners in both 1911 and 1921. After a decade, the figure remarkably fell to about 10,000 in 1931 and remained stable in 1941. From 1951 to 1971, the male prison population rose continuously to 19,000 in 1951 and 20,000 in 1971. In the last two decades, the number of male prisoners had a continued upturn to 38,000 in 1981 and followed by 45,000 in 2001, remarking the highest point of the entire chart.

As for women, the figure for female prison population started at north of 3,000 in 1911 and south of 2,000 in 1921. After that, the figure had a consider drop to around 500 prisoners 10 years ago. From 1951 to 1961, female prison population slightly increased between 900 and 1,500. However, it still decreased to downward of 1,000 over the next two decades. At the end of the period, there was a gradual growth; meanwhile, not much, around 2,000 prisoners in 2001.

Regarding categories with lower data, 150 grams, the amount of lamb used in a European country went down progressively by about 100 grams over 25 years. The figures for the consumption of fish remained stable during the former half of the period; however, there was a slight drop to 40 grams in the end of the period, marking the lowest point of this chart.

The bar chart illustrates how much young people in higher education in four countries A, B, C and D over a 10-year period, commencing from 2000.

Overall, all the studied nations witnessed signs of growth in people having higher education. Also of note is that the country D had the highest figures throughout the years.

Regarding categories with remaining countries, the share of younger people in hogher education in country B remained stable at 40% throughout the years; however, there was a lower figure in 2005, about 38%. The figures for country C also had a slight rise from 50% to 53% between 2000 and 2010.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates how many woman attendants of parliament in five European countries labeled as Germany, Italy, France, UK and Belgium over a 12-year period, commencing from 2000.

Overall, there was a general increase in the proportion of female members of parliament in the studied nations. Also of note is that the figures for the UK had the most dramatic growth from 2000 to 2012.

To elaborate, in Germany, about 34% woman participated in parliament in 2000, with a slight rice to 37% in 2012. The figures for Italy had a considerable upward trend from 26% in 2000 to 39% in 2012, marking the highest point of the entire chart.

Regarding the remaining, in 2000, an impressive 25% of female attendants was reported in France. This number; however, rose remarkably to 37% in 2004 before decreasing gradually from 29% to 32% in the latter half of the period. The figures for Belgium had a dramatic growth between 16% and 24% in the former of the period, then fall slightly to 23% in 2012. Finally, the share of woman attended to parliament in the UK witnessed the highest increase with just under 5% going up to 28% in 2012; however, they still remained lower figures than 4 nations surveyed over the whole timeline.

reviews.originalEssay:
The pie charts illustrate why students in the UK decided to study in a particular university in 1997 and 2007. 

Overall, out of the studied reasons, suitable degree courses is the most important reason in both 1996 and 2007. Also of note is that the proportion of proximity to parental homes had a dramatic growth between 1997 and 2007. 

To elaborate, only 10% of proximity to parental home was choosen by students in the Uk, with a dramatic growth to 22% in 2007. The figures for suitable degree courses increased slightly from 35% to 37% over the period, reaching the highest figures of the entire chart. 

Regarding categories with lower data, the proportion of quality of resources witnessed signs of drop from 21% to 17% over a 10-year period. Likewise, the figures for quality of teaching rose steadily about 3% throughout the years. Finally, there was 19% of good sports and social activities, with a remarkable fall to 6% in the end of the period, ranking the lowest figure in 2007.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The pie charts show how students' reasons for choosing a particular university in the UK varied between 1997 and 2007, with each reason expressed as a percentage of students.

Overall, the percentages for suitable degree courses, proximity to parental home and quality of teaching rose, whereas those for quality of resources and good sports and social activities fell. Suitable degree courses remained the leading reason in both years, while sports and social activities became the least common in 2007.

To elaborate, in 1997, 10% of students chose their university because it was close to their parental home, with this figure rising to 22% in 2007. The proportion citing suitable degree courses was much higher, increasing slightly from 35% to 37% over the same period and remaining the largest share in each year.

Regarding the remaining reasons, 21% of students cited the quality of resources in 1997, compared with 17% in 2007. By contrast, the percentage citing quality of teaching rose from 15% to 18%, a gain of three percentage points. Finally, the share choosing the university for its good sports and social activities dropped from 19% to 6%, the lowest figure in 2007.
